title: OrCam computer-vision readers improve daily-living task performance in independent clinical cohorts (2015-2023)
summary: Independent cohorts (12, 100, 6 and 10 participants) show OrCam devices raising reading and daily-task scores; no individual outcome.
account: Independent clinical studies of OrCam's wearable and handheld text-and-object readers report cohort gains. In a US ophthalmology department between 1 July and 30 September 2015, 12 patients with acuity of 20/200 or worse improved on a 10-item daily-living test from 2.5 to 9.5 with the device at the first visit and 9.8 after a week of use at home (JAMA Ophthalmology, 2016). A five-center study of 100 users found improved reading and face recognition (Journal of Medical Systems, 2023). Six UC Davis patients with stroke or brain tumors used OrCam Read for a month in 2021 (Neuro-Ophthalmology, 2024), and at the NIH nine children with CLN3 disease completed all level-A text, color and face tasks by day five (Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2026). No individual outcome is attributed.
purpose: Read text and recognize faces, objects and colors aloud for people with visual impairment
system: OrCam MyEye, MyEye 2 and OrCam Read (camera-based optical character and object recognition with audio output)
model_version: OrCam (2015 study; model not named in the abstract); OrCam MyEye (2023 multicentre study); OrCam MyEye 2 (NIH); OrCam Read (UC Davis)
deployer: Study clinics: a US ophthalmology department (2015), five vision rehabilitation centers, UC Davis Ophthalmology, NIH Clinical Center
segment: People with low vision, acquired brain injury or CLN3 disease

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: outcomes are cohort means on daily-living and task tests; no individual beneficiary is identified.
General benefit without an event: multi-site cohort evidence of usability, not an attributable societal outcome.

ai_role.statement: The devices' computer-vision recognition of text, faces and colors is the function measured in every study; comparisons were against no aid or existing low-vision aids, and the 2016 test instrument was non-validated, so effects are task-level rather than clinical outcomes.

paired_incident.title: Error-Prone AI Accessibility Tools Reportedly Lead to Navigation Issues for Blind Internet Users
paired_incident.basis: Both are vendor AI products sold to recognize and read content aloud for low-vision users; the overlays' inaccurate descriptions degraded rather than improved daily task performance for blind and visually impaired users.

headline: OrCam readers raise daily-living test scores from 2.5 to 9.5
metric: improved on a 10-item daily-living test from 2.5 to 9.5
